conviction_note: Near-balanced: the one new document since the last print is the listed subsidiary Fujiya halving its FY operating-profit plan on 10/26 (a 1.6bn yen hole against Yamazaki's 64bn plan, plus a read-through on Q3 consumer restraint and packaging and energy costs). Against it sit the first full quarter of the July 5.6% price rise, which the company said in July held volumes, and a street FY number about 2% above plan. With a +7.3% 20-day run-in and a margin ratio below 1 pulling both ways, p_up is 47 on a 3.5% scale. The findings sum (-0.25) and the scaled number (-0.21) agree in sign and size.

Margin ratio 0.64: margin shorts exceed margin longs, the setup that squeezes on good news, not a crowded long. 20-day run-up +7.31%, and +16% since the H1 print (3,359 on 2026-07-31 to 3,907). findings.finding: Consolidated listed subsidiary Fujiya (2211) cut its FY2026 operating-profit forecast from 3,200m to 1,600m yen (-50%) on 2026-10-26. Its Q3 standalone OP was -410m against -133m a year earlier: 9M OP was -113m and H1 was +297m. It cited record prolonged rain, torrential rain, the Kumamoto earthquake, stronger consumer thrift in response to food price rises, and packaging and energy costs above plan because of the Middle East. Yamazaki's own FY plan carries Fujiya at 3,200m OP (H1 supplementary, p.6), so the cut is a ~1.6bn (2.5%) hole in the consolidated 64bn plan, about 54% of it attributable after minorities. It also makes a Q3 upward revision by Yamazaki less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance line: in 2025 the Q3 print carried an upward FY revision (57,500 to 59,000 OP) and the stock still fell 4.04% after a -6% run-in. At H1 2026 the plan was held, ordinary profit missed IFIS by 1.1%, and the stock fell 1.55%. In 2023 and 2024 Q3 held the plan (+0.56%, +15.31%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it came out at 15:30 yesterday and Yamazaki is down about 1.2% this morning while Fujiya itself is only -1.3%. What is not priced is how Yamazaki's own Q3 absorbs it: Fujiya is about 5% of the consolidated plan, and the -277m Q3 YoY drag is about 2.8% of last year's Q3 consolidated OP (10,028m). The same release carries cost and consumer read-throughs for Yamazaki's 和洋菓子 and 製菓 lines. If it were fully priced, the street FY number (68,300m ordinary) would have come down toward or below the 67,000m plan. It has not been updated since the 10/26 release.
findings.independence: The Fujiya Q3 短信 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261026/140120261013549981.pdf) gives the 9M OP of -113m. It is the same issuer and the same day, so it counts as one finding. Yamazaki's H1 supplementary (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260731/140120260730504016.pdf) independently shows Fujiya H1 OP falling from 1,202m to 297m and its plan of 3,200m.

findings.finding: Q3 (Jul-Sep) is the first full quarter of Yamazaki's price rise on 306 items from 1 July 2026 shipments (average +5.6%; 食パン +6.6%, 菓子パン +5.0%, 和洋菓子 +6.4%). In the H1 短信 the company wrote that thanks to its preparation and the quality upgrades it 販売数量確保を実現し、業績は順調に推移しております, i.e. it held sales volumes through July after the rise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quarter line: Q1 2026 ordinary profit beat IFIS by 2.1% and the stock rose 2.12%. H1 missed by 1.1% and it fell 1.55%. Q3 2024 (OP +39% YoY cumulative) rose 15.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The rise was announced on 2026-04-28 and the volume comment was published on 07-31, and the stock has risen 16% since. What remains is the size of the margin recovery in the quarter itself, after Q2 standalone OP slipped to 17,521m from Q1's 18,328m. Nobody outside the company sees that before the print because Yamazaki publishes no 月次.
findings.independence: Price-rise detail: https://pricey.jp/web/articles/4917 (snippet only). The Oanda/Kyodo item 'ロイヤルブレッド値上げへ', https://www.oanda.jp/lab-education/market_news/kn_2026042801002032/ (snippet only). Both are the same 4/28 announcement, so this counts once.

findings.finding: The bar has risen into the print. IFIS FY ordinary consensus is 68,300m against the 67,000m plan, a US broker went to Buy with a 4,600 target on 2026-10-22, and the stock is +7.3% over 20 days and +16% since the H1 print. Yamazaki raised at Q3 in only one of the last three years (2025 yes; 2023 and 2024 held), so a held plan is the base case and would leave the street above the company for the second print running.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a -6% run-in, the 2025 Q3 raise was sold -4.04%. After a -5.8% run-in, Q3 2024 held the plan and rose 15.31%. Every prior Q3 came after a decline, and this is the first one after a rise.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: possible, not the base case. The plan was held at Q1 and H1, IFIS ordinary is 1.9% above plan, Fujiya's -1.6bn cut opens a hole, and Yamazaki raised at Q3 in 1 of 3 years. Returns: none expected at Q3 by the company's own record (January dividend revisions, February buybacks). New-year guide: not applicable at Q3. Quarter: H1 ordinary progress was 56.5% against 57.6% last year (IFIS). The plan needs H2 OP +6.4% YoY against H1's +3.3%, so Q3 has to show the price rise working; last year's Q3 cumulative ordinary progress was 75.3% of the revised plan.

baseline_tension: The baseline's priced lean is -0.27, mostly the run-up term, and what I found is close to it. A small negative from the Fujiya cut, which the price is already partly taking this morning, is set against the first price-rise quarter. The strongest positive the release could carry is a Q3 upward FY revision like 2025's (consensus sits above plan); I looked for it. It is plausible but not the base case after Fujiya's cut, and a buyback or dividend change at Q3 has no precedent in this company's last two years.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative on a series the market already has): the Fujiya revision is public since 10/26 15:30 and partly in this morning's -1.2%, so the finding went from -0.5 to -0.4 and p_up from 45 to 47
Open question 4 (a run-in sized as a short lost once): the run-up finding went from -0.3 to -0.15, also because the margin ratio of 0.64 is short-heavy
Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): the strongest positive (a Q3 upward revision) is written into baseline_tension. I had already looked for it, so it moved nothing further
